title: Starter experiments: SDK quickloop patterns
body:
Goal
---
Create a tiny, repeatable onramp for engineers to get from zero to a validated SDK integration in under 30 minutes. Focus on enabling fast experiments ("quickloops") that exercise telemetry and a minimal production-like request path so we can iterate on SDK ergonomics and common failure modes.

Why this differs from other docs
---
- Not a full bootcamp: focused micro-experiments developers can run in ~5–30 minutes.
- Telemetry-first: each quickloop emits a curated minimal telemetry set so we can measure first-run success signals.
- Preset-driven: provide 3 opinionated presets (starter, performance, guarded) developers can toggle.

Quickloop patterns (3 canonical flows)
---
1) Hello-gen quickloop (5–10m)
   - intent: confirm end-to-end generation using hosted API with minimal config.
   - steps: create API key, install sdk, run hello-gen example, verify token-level telemetry appears in console.
   - success signals: response returned within timeout, telemetry: request_id, model, latency_ms, tokens_out.

2) Local-stub smoke (10–20m)
   - intent: reproduce real network errors locally and validate graceful retry/fallback.
   - steps: run the included local stub (docker compose minimal) that simulates 5% 503s and slow responses; run sample client to exercise backoff and fallback: fallback to small-model variant.
   - success signals: client recorded retry_count, final_status, fallback_used=true when simulated capacity tight.

3) Prompt-eval loop (20–30m)
   - intent: run a tiny eval of 10 prompts to catch immediate regressions after a model/version switch.
   - steps: run prompt-suite script, compare quality metric (e.g., normalized BLEU/heuristic score) against baseline stored in /examples/baselines. If regression > threshold, auto-flag in telemetry.
   - success signals: eval pass/fail, prompt_mismatch_count, avg_confidence_score.

Presets (opinionated configs)
---
- starter: low-cost, 1 request concurrency, default quantized model, no batch. Good for initial dev runs.
- performance: higher concurrency, batching enabled (batch_size=8), KV-cache warmed, for throughput testing.
- guarded: strict timeouts (200ms token), retries with exponential backoff, local-stub integration, for near-prod safe tests.

Minimal telemetry schema (always emitted by example clients)
---
- request_id (string)
- timestamp (iso8601)
- owner_email (string) - optional in local runs
- env (starter|performance|guarded)
- model (string)
- model_version (string)
- latency_ms (number as string)
- tokens_in (number as string)
- tokens_out (number as string)
- status (ok|error|fallback)
- error_code (if any)
- retry_count
- fallback_used (true|false)

Note: above values are emitted as strings in the quick example JSON to avoid schema mismatch when plumbing into varied telemetry backends.

CLI quickstart (copy-paste)
---
- install: pip install redwood-sdk-preview
- configure: redwood config set --api-key $REDWOOD_KEY --env starter
- run hello: python examples/hello_gen.py --model small-alpha
- run eval: python examples/prompt_eval.py --suite examples/prompt_suites/basic.json --baseline examples/baselines/basic.json

Example safety fallback heuristics (in client)
---
- if latency_ms > env_threshold then: enable batch-size=1, reduce max_tokens to 64
- on 503 or timeout: exponential backoff 200ms->800ms->1.6s, then call fallback_model("small-alpha-quant")
- if 5 failures in a minute: mark route degraded=true and emit alert telemetry tag route_degraded

Developer UX scripts included
---
- scripts/quickloop.sh — runs Hello-gen then Prompt-eval, aggregates telemetry to local ./tmp/telemetry.json for mock ingestion.
- scripts/start-stub.sh — starts dockerized stub server that simulates network conditions.
- examples/telemetry_preview.ipynb — lightweight notebook to load ./tmp/telemetry.json and show first-run metrics (latency histogram, success rate).

Onboarding checklist for a first-time integrator (10–30m)
---
- [ ] create account & API key (5m)
- [ ] run hello-gen (5m)
- [ ] confirm telemetry appears in Console > Live (2m)
- [ ] run local-stub and simulate error (5–10m)
- [ ] toggle to guarded preset and run prompt-eval (5–10m)

Instrumenter notes for eng-dx (what to monitor)
---
- First-run success rate (percentage of hello-gen runs that complete without manual intervention). Target: >= 85%.
- Telemetry ingestion latency (how long till we see request_id in Console). Target: < 10s for hosted.
- Average time-to-flag for prompt-eval regressions when baseline changes. Goal: < 1 hour from rollout.

Open questions / follow-ups
---
- Which baseline storage is allowed for public examples? S3 vs in-repo small JSON? (security/size tradeoffs)
- Should the quickloop scripts auto-open a small browser to Console with the request_id prefiltered? (UX improvement)
- Does commercial docs need a trimmed version of telemetry emitted (PII concerns)?

Next steps (proposed short roadmap)
---
- Week 0: land hello-gen + telemetry wiring example + one-pager (this doc)
- Week 1: add local-stub and guarded preset, internal testing across 5 teams
- Week 2: iterate telemetry keys (add minimal cost metrics) and make quickloop.sh idempotent
- Week 3: integrate with console demo link and prepare customer-facing trimmed variant

Notes to self / rough TODOs
---
- make sample API key ephemeral and limited-scope for demo org
- add a single-line troubleshooting FAQ for common mac/linux networking gotchas
- record 2-minute screencast of quickloop (for advocates)
- follow up with security on telemetry sampling rates

End.
